info.title: FleetFuel Portal API
info.description: REST API of the FleetFuel Portal, a fictional portfolio project. Every operation is served and checked against real responses by tests/Feature/Api/OpenApiContractTest.php and the per-endpoint API tests; x-abilities (all required), x-any-abilities (at least one required) and x-roles are compared with the route middleware, and x-status records that each operation is implemented. Business details: docs/04-BUSINESS-RULES.md and docs/05-API-CONTRACT.md.

patch.summary: Admin or own manager updates quotas/status
patch.description: A nonempty subset of monthly_limit_l, monthly_limit_usd (decimal strings, null = unlimited) and status (active or blocked), applied together under the card lock and audited. A limit may drop below this month's usage. Ownership, assignment and card number cannot change here (422). Archived cards are final: 409 invalid_transition. An inactive company's limits cannot change and its cards cannot be unblocked: 403 company_inactive. Another company's card is 404.

patch.description: expected_status is the status the caller last saw; status is the target. The order row is locked, then: a company manager may only ask for pending -> cancelled on their own order (anything else 403 forbidden); if the order is no longer in expected_status the change is refused with 409 stale_state (details.current_status); a skipped step, the same status again or any move out of delivered/cancelled is 409 invalid_transition. Scheduling needs scheduled_start_at (future, at most 366 days ahead), scheduled_end_at (after the start) and assigned_truck; cancelling needs reason; these fields are refused for other targets (422). delivered_at is set from server time. Each accepted change writes one history row and one audit row in the same transaction. Token: an admin needs deliveries:status, a company manager deliveries:write; the route accepts either and the request checks the one the role needs (403).

get.description: One row per company, vehicle or product (group_by, default company), grouped by ID so equal names never merge; largest liters first, then group_id with null last. Sums of the liters and LBP/USD amounts stored with each purchase: nothing is repriced. Grouping by vehicle uses the vehicle recorded on the purchase, and card-only purchases form one group with group_id null. from/to are Beirut dates [from, to), at most 366 days, default the current Beirut month. An admin may filter by company_id; a manager sees their own company and company_id is refused (422). fleet_id keeps only the purchases paid with that fleet's cards, and must belong to the filtered company (admin) or the caller's company (manager). Unknown parameters are 422. Unpaginated.

get.description: Every purchase the caller may see that matches the filters of GET /transactions, without pagination (page and per_page are refused, 422), oldest first by (transacted_at, id). UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, a header row, then the columns transaction_id, external_ref, company, vehicle_plate, station, product_code, liters, unit_price_lbp, amount_lbp, amount_usd, rate_source, transacted_at_utc. Amounts are the stored snapshots. Text cells that start with =, +, - or @ (also after spaces), a tab or a line break get a leading apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas. Content-Type text/csv; charset=UTF-8; Content-Disposition attachment.
The authenticated user's own in-app inbox, newest first, optionally filtered by read state and event type.
